I think we want it to be a string, so that it's easy to return from the getter/set from the setter; otherwise we'd have to do a bunch of identity-ish conversions between strings and "abstract CSS property values". body:
Yes, these are the values currently used by the implementers. I believe the section [canvas compositing and blending](https://drafts.fxtf.org/compositing/#canvascompositingandblending) is the one that does rule here. Only the "normal" blending mode is not supported by any vendor and I doubt it will ever; WebKit is the only one already supporting the new "plus-lighter" and "plus-darker" composite modes (though [Blink is apparently on it](https://groups.google.com/a/chromium.org/g/blink-dev/c/0ngoiUCAdE8/m/OjYQRp1yCgAJ?pli=1)); and Gecko is the only one that still doesn't support the "clear" compositing mode.  
Should we add an ", or is not supported by the UA" clause to allow the UAs to ignore some of these but not let them accept any other?

body:
Oh! There is actually an interop issue here. For Chrome (and maybe WebKit since they have the same behavior), the thing is that it's either <composite mode> + <blend:"normal"> or <composite:"source-over"> + <blend mode>. And at getting if we have <blend:"normal"> they return the composite mode.  
This means that they do actually accept the input `"normal"` but it maps to `"source-over"` at getting.  
Firefox on the other hand seems to ignore `"normal"` completely.  
Here is a small test: https://jsfiddle.net/necuLt90/
Based on this, I fear it becomes more than an editorial change and maybe we should ask some inputs from @whatwg/canvas?
